newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Native groups in Argentina for environment meeting.
newsitem.headline: Native groups in Argentina for environment meeting.

text.p: Representatives of indigenous peoples from three continents will meet in Argentina this weekend to prepare a proposal for the international biodiversity conference in November.

The International Indigenous Biodiversity Forum said on Thursday that native leaders from South America, Africa and Asia would meet to discuss how best to protect the diversity of the world's plant and animal life.

"If the environment suffers, it is the native peoples who suffer most," said forum spokesman Rodolfo Asar. He said that 30 indigenous leaders would attend from abroad along with 100 Argentine Indians.
The forum will present its proposals to representatives of world governments meeting in Buenos Aires on Nov. 4-15 for the third conference of the World Biological Diversity Convention.
The Biodiversity Convention was an outcome of the 1992 Earth Summit in Rio de Janiero.
